recommendation: Keep the external-repo audit as-is. No core follow-up is indicated unless a future final decision brings Permission back into core; future Permission maturity and identifier changes should be made in HL7/data-access-policies.
issue_request: FHIR-46461 was an Applied/Persuasive Security work group issue for R6 requesting that the Permission resource be elevated to FMM 1. Jira's application comment noted that identifier needed to be added to satisfy FMM 1 requirements.
initial_application: Commit 58a264be3617c318e637f060d5f9901eb17ddcbb, merged by HL7/fhir#3124 as c47a45a0c1ceceda1ecab8a4da2664a494f0323d, changed source/fhir.ini from permission=0 to permission=1, added Permission.identifier to source/permission/structuredefinition-Permission.xml, added an identifier search parameter, and added FiveWs mapping exceptions.
additional_context: Commit 0e2a8a7f839d5e1a43787523daccf07d958362f3 later removed source/permission and the active source/fhir.ini Permission entries from core. Current source/secpriv-module.html links Permission to the HL7 Data Access Policies IG, and the FMG Zulip resource-removal thread records Security's agreement to move Permission out of core. The current HL7/data-access-policies Permission source still has structuredefinition-fmm value 1 and a Permission.identifier element.
reconciliation: No core source change was made. Reintroducing the removed core Permission resource or fhir.ini entries would conflict with the later source-of-truth move, while the external Permission source already preserves the FHIR-46461 application.
